      "title": "Clarify MCP authorization permissions and workspace identity",
      "url": "https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-4/clarify-mcp-authorization-permissions-and-workspace-identity",
      "description": "## Executive summary\n\nImprove Skillplane's MCP OAuth authorization page so people can understand exactly what every requested permission permits, see which Skillplane identity is granting access, and understand which workspace or set of workspaces the authorization applies to. Where the authorization model permits it, allow the user to select or switch the target workspace before granting access.\n\n## Problem or opportunity\n\nThe current authorization page communicates the client and MCP resource, but parts of the consent are ambiguous:\n\n* Some scopes have useful explanations, while `skills:write` and `skills:publish` display the generic text \u201cUse this Skillplane permission.\u201d\n* The page does not clearly identify the signed-in Skillplane user/account that will grant access.\n* A user with multiple workspaces cannot tell whether the token applies to one workspace, the currently selected workspace, or every workspace they can access.\n* There is no visible way to switch the relevant account or workspace before authorizing, when such scoping is supported.\n* Generic or unclear permission copy makes least-privilege review harder and increases the chance of approving broader access than intended.\n\n## Expected outcome\n\nThe consent screen becomes a trustworthy authorization decision surface: every scope has precise action-oriented copy, the authenticating identity is explicit, and workspace reach is stated accurately. If workspace-bound consent is technically supportable, the user can select the intended workspace and the issued authorization enforces that selection.\n\n## Goals\n\n* Provide specific descriptions for every supported OAuth scope.\n* Display the authenticated Skillplane user in a privacy-conscious form.\n* Explain the workspace reach of the authorization before consent.\n* Explore and, if supported safely, implement workspace selection or switching.\n* Preserve PKCE, redirect URI safety messaging, least privilege, and existing OAuth/MCP interoperability.\n* Add accessibility, responsive-layout, authorization, and regression coverage.\n\n## Non-goals\n\n* Redesign unrelated Skillplane authentication or account settings.\n* Change the meaning of existing scopes without a separately reviewed authorization migration.\n* Change service-principal credential behavior.\n* Imply workspace isolation in the UI unless it is enforced in the token and server authorization path.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] Every requested scope displays concise, action-specific copy. At minimum, `skills:write` explains skill creation and skill-record management, and `skills:publish` explains review approval and publication.\n- [ ] The consent screen shows which Skillplane user/account is authenticated without exposing unnecessary personal data.\n- [ ] The screen accurately states whether access covers one workspace or all workspaces available to the user.\n- [ ] The current workspace context, if one exists, is visibly identified.\n- [ ] Workspace switching/selection feasibility is evaluated against the OAuth token, audience/resource, authorization-code, and server-side workspace-enforcement model.\n- [ ] If workspace selection is implemented, the selected workspace is enforced server-side, cannot be changed silently, and is represented in auditable authorization state.\n- [ ] If workspace-bound authorization is not feasible in the current model, the UI clearly explains multi-workspace reach and offers an explicit account/workspace management path instead of a misleading selector.\n- [ ] Consent, denial, relogin, revoked access, multi-workspace, single-workspace, and stale-session flows are tested.\n- [ ] The page remains keyboard accessible, screen-reader understandable, and responsive.\n- [ ] Security copy continues to identify the MCP resource and warn about the local callback destination without leaking tokens, authorization codes, or private identifiers.\n\n## Dependencies and risks\n\n* AuthFn OAuth consent rendering and client metadata.\n* Skillplane workspace membership and authorization model.\n* Scope-to-tool/action mapping as the source of permission descriptions.\n* Token claims or grants if consent becomes workspace-bound.\n* Existing Codex, Linear, ChatGPT, and other MCP client compatibility.\n* Risk: a visual workspace selector without token-level enforcement would create false assurance.\n* Risk: disclosing an email or workspace membership list may expose more identity information than necessary.\n\n## Open questions\n\n* Does the current OAuth grant authorize a user across all accessible workspaces, or can it be bound to one workspace without breaking MCP discovery?\n* Should \u201cswitch workspace\u201d change token scope, choose a domain context for the session, or only navigate account settings?\n* Which user identifier is appropriate on consent: display name, masked email, avatar, or account ID?\n* Should scope descriptions be static product copy or generated from a canonical scope/action registry?\n* How should consent behave when membership changes after authorization?",

      "id": "ca2b8cef-87c0-47cc-b122-15789ab80687",
      "identifier": "SKI-9",
      "title": "Adopt mdfn across Skillplane web editing surfaces",
      "url": "https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-9/adopt-mdfn-across-skillplane-web-editing-surfaces",
      "description": "## Executive summary\n\nAdopt mdfn as Skillplane's shared Markdown editor and renderer for the five Markdown authoring flows verified in the current source:\n\n1. New-skill `SKILL.md`\n2. Amend-current-skill `SKILL.md`\n3. Initial context knowledge\n4. Context knowledge revisions\n5. Context note creation and revisions\n\nThis is a consumer integration of [SFN-20 \u2014 Build mdfn as the Superfunctions Markdown authoring platform](<https://linear.app/21n/issue/SFN-20/build-mdfn-as-the-superfunctions-markdown-authoring-platform>). It must not reimplement the mdfn engine or replace Skillplane's current domain workflows.\n\n## Source-verified baseline\n\nAudited read-only on 2026-08-12:\n\n* Skillplane checkout: `45733752797a5de552a447560983d24a9d02bcd1`\n* Refreshed `origin/main`: `ccf8966fc66900d2c5f1f0b2efbe514a1ed93ff6`\n* The inspected editor, renderer, API, domain, and test paths are identical across those revisions.\n* No mdfn dependency or implementation currently exists in Skillplane.\n* Existing baseline passed: app unit tests 3/3 and domain unit tests 30/30 with pnpm 11.9.0.\n\nThe earlier generic inventory is now resolved to concrete source paths and lifecycle contracts below.\n\n## Verified integration map\n\n| Surface | Current source | Existing persistence semantics |\n| -- | -- | -- |\n| New skill instructions | `app/src/routes/(app)/[workspaceSlug]/skills/new/+page.svelte` | Builds a deterministic bundle containing required `SKILL.md` and generated `skill.json`; creates immutable published v1.0.0 |\n| Amend skill instructions | `app/src/lib/skills/SkillEditor.svelte` | Loads the current immutable base bundle, replaces only `SKILL.md`, rebuilds generated metadata, and creates a `pending_review` candidate using `baseVersionId`, semantic bump, and idempotency |\n| Initial context knowledge | `app/src/lib/contexts/ContextEditor.svelte` | Creates a context with immutable knowledge revision 1 through the existing flow |\n| Knowledge revision | `app/src/lib/contexts/KnowledgeEditor.svelte` | Creates an immutable next revision using `expectedRevision` and idempotency; stale writes return `CONTEXT_REVISION_CONFLICT` |\n| Context note | `app/src/lib/contexts/NoteEditor.svelte` | Creates a note or immutable next note revision; updates use `expectedRevision` and idempotency; stale writes return `NOTE_REVISION_CONFLICT` |\n| Read-only Markdown | `packages/ui/src/SafeMarkdown.svelte` and `packages/ui/src/markdown.ts` | Shared rendering for current content and immutable skill/knowledge/note history |\n\n## Scope\n\n### In scope\n\n* One shared Skillplane Markdown editor wrapper with source, visual, split, preview, read-only, diagnostics, and safe source fallback.\n* One named mdfn parsing/rendering/security profile shared by editor preview and `SafeMarkdown`.\n* Replace the five verified Markdown textareas while retaining their existing parent components.\n* Preserve the current `SafeMarkdown` and `renderSafeMarkdown` public APIs while migrating their internals.\n* Lazy-load browser editing code at editable Svelte boundaries; keep read-only rendering environment-neutral and SSR-safe.\n* Feature switches and rollback per surface.\n* Preservation, security, accessibility, E2E, SSR, performance, IME, clipboard, large-document, and conflict-recovery coverage.\n\n### Explicitly out of scope\n\n* Descriptions, change summaries, learning summaries, review/rejection reasons, JSON metadata, titles, names, slugs, labels, identifiers, and external references.\n* Editing bundle files other than `SKILL.md` in the first release.\n* Changing API/MCP request or response shapes.\n* Changing database schemas or migrating stored Markdown.\n* Replacing authorization, domain services, audits, revision storage, bundle construction, review, or publication.\n* Autosaving domain mutations. Current saves create immutable versions/revisions and remain explicit.\n* Making published or historical records mutable.\n* Implementing mdfn core packages inside Skillplane.\n\n## Architecture boundary\n\n```\nexisting page or dialog\n  -> shared MarkdownEditor.svelte\n       -> mdfn browser adapter\n       -> emits canonical Markdown string\n  -> existing submit handler\n  -> existing API client\n  -> existing domain service/transaction\n  -> immutable bundle, version, or revision\n```\n\nThe editor does not receive resource IDs, authorization policy, idempotency keys, revision tokens, publication actions, or archive actions. Existing parent components continue to own those responsibilities.\n\nRendering retains the current compatibility boundary:\n\n```\ncanonical Markdown\n  -> shared mdfn profile\n  -> environment-neutral safe renderer\n  -> SafeMarkdown\n```\n\n## Required invariants\n\n### Skill creation and amendments\n\n* `SKILL.md` remains canonical bundle content.\n* New-skill creation continues to publish immutable v1.0.0 through the current API.\n* Amendments continue to preserve non-entrypoint files, rebuild generated `skill.json`, and submit a deterministic archive.\n* The server continues to canonicalize and validate the bundle.\n* Candidate creation continues to verify the base is current, reject identical bundles, and create `pending_review`.\n* Publication remains a separate `skills:publish` action.\n* Historical versions and non-entrypoint files remain read-only.\n* Current UI source cap remains 1,048,576 characters; compressed bundle cap remains 10 MiB.\n\n### Context knowledge\n\n* The canonical submitted string is preserved exactly after non-empty and byte-size validation.\n* Knowledge body limit remains 512 KiB.\n* `expectedRevision`, idempotency, transaction locks, authorization, archived-state checks, immutable revision insert, current pointer, and audit event remain unchanged.\n* A conflict never silently overwrites remote data or automatically discards the local source.\n\n### Context notes\n\n* Title and lifecycle remain separate from the Markdown body.\n* Note body limit remains 256 KiB; active-note limit remains 500 per context.\n* Create/update branching, expected revision, idempotency, immutable history, authorization, archive restrictions, and audits remain unchanged.\n* Archive/unarchive remains a separate domain action.\n\n### Rendering and security\n\nThe new profile must equal or exceed the current renderer:\n\n* Raw HTML is not executed.\n* Unsafe schemes and protocol-relative URLs are rejected.\n* Safe relative, fragment, HTTP, HTTPS, and mail links behave according to policy.\n* External links receive safe attributes.\n* Images and future embeds use explicit policy.\n* Markdown bodies never enter analytics or crash-event properties.\n* Editor and read-only rendering do not drift onto different profiles.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] The five verified Markdown inputs use the shared wrapper; no plain-text or JSON field is migrated.\n- [ ] `SafeMarkdown` and `renderSafeMarkdown` retain their application-facing APIs and use the same mdfn profile as preview.\n- [ ] Browser editing code is client-only and lazy-loaded; SSR/read-only pages remain useful without it.\n- [ ] Loading, no-edit mode switching, failed editor loading, and fallback preserve the current Markdown string.\n- [ ] Unsupported syntax remains recoverable in source mode and produces actionable diagnostics.\n- [ ] New-skill creation still produces a deterministic valid bundle and published immutable v1.0.0.\n- [ ] Skill amendments preserve all non-`SKILL.md` files and still produce the correct candidate/review/publication lifecycle.\n- [ ] Knowledge and note saves preserve size limits, `expectedRevision`, idempotency, immutable history, authorization, archived-state checks, current pointers, and audit behavior.\n- [ ] Stale conflicts retain local source until explicit reload/reapply.\n- [ ] Existing raw-HTML, unsafe-link, external-link, and deterministic-bundle unit tests remain green and are expanded for profile parity and preservation.\n- [ ] `packages/testing/e2e/skills.spec.ts` covers create, amend, diff, publish, bundle preservation, source fallback, viewer, and historical read-only behavior.\n- [ ] `packages/testing/e2e/contexts.spec.ts` covers initial knowledge, immutable revision, stale conflict/recovery, note create/edit/history/archive, and viewer behavior.\n- [ ] Accessibility coverage includes keyboard, focus, labels, screen readers, mobile, IME/composition, and clipboard.\n- [ ] Large-document, adversarial-content, SSR/hydration, bundle-cost, ambiguous-save, and per-surface rollback tests pass.\n- [ ] Existing API, domain, E2E, visual, accessibility, agent-facing retrieval, and audit regression suites remain green.\n- [ ] No database/content migration is required, and disabling a surface restores the current source control over the same canonical Markdown.\n\n## Delivery sequence\n\n### Phase 0 \u2014 mdfn conformance spike\n\nResolve supported public package versions from [SFN-20](https://linear.app/21n/issue/SFN-20/build-mdfn-as-the-superfunctions-markdown-authoring-platform). Prove Svelte support, environment-neutral rendering, SSR-safe browser entrypoints, preservation guarantees, diagnostics, security hooks, and source fallback against real Skillplane fixtures.\n\n### Phase 1 \u2014 shared profile, renderer, and wrapper\n\nAdd the named profile, migrate `renderSafeMarkdown` internally, add the app-level shared editor and source fallback, and port current renderer-security tests. Keep renderer/editor rollout independently switchable.\n\n### Phase 2 \u2014 skills\n\nMigrate new-skill and skill-amendment `SKILL.md`. Verify deterministic bundles, preservation of other files, current-base conflict behavior, candidate creation, review/publication separation, viewer state, historical read-only state, and rollback.\n\n### Phase 3 \u2014 contexts\n\nMigrate initial knowledge, knowledge revisions, and note bodies. Verify byte limits, immutable revisions, expected-revision conflicts, local-source recovery, archive behavior, viewers, history, and rollback.\n\n### Phase 4 \u2014 hardening and rollout\n\nRun browser, accessibility, mobile, IME, clipboard, adversarial-content, large-document, SSR, performance, recovery, and rollback gates. Roll out independently per surface and capture only redacted categorical metrics.\n\n## Dependency and risks\n\n* [SFN-20](<https://linear.app/21n/issue/SFN-20/build-mdfn-as-the-superfunctions-markdown-authoring-platform>) is a hard dependency for stable public parsing, rendering, browser editing, Svelte, preservation, diagnostics, extension, security, and test contracts.\n* Exact mdfn package names are intentionally not guessed; resolve them from supported releases before implementation.\n* Source normalization can change bundle digests or create misleading revisions.\n* Importing browser code into read-only paths can break SSR and increase initial bundles.\n* Broad textarea replacement would corrupt field semantics; only the verified Markdown inputs are in scope.\n* Autosave can create unintended immutable records and is excluded.\n* Client/server profile drift can make previews inaccurate.\n* Local recovery and observability can leak private context unless bodies are excluded.\n* Dependency instability is isolated behind the thin wrapper and version pinning.\n\n## Definition of ready\n\n* [SFN-20](https://linear.app/21n/issue/SFN-20/build-mdfn-as-the-superfunctions-markdown-authoring-platform) exposes stable supported public entrypoints for the required capabilities.\n* Its preservation and security guarantees pass Skillplane's real fixtures.\n* Shared wrapper/profile contracts and independent feature switches are approved.\n* The green baseline is reproducible with the repository runtime.\n* [SKI-9](https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-9/adopt-mdfn-across-skillplane-web-editing-surfaces) is explicitly prioritized from Backlog.\n\n## Associated documents\n\n* [Ideation & Product Rationale \u2014 SKI-9](<https://linear.app/21n/document/ideation-and-product-rationale-ski-9-adopt-mdfn-across-skillplane-web-bdf7504606c6>)\n* [Architecture & Delivery Plan \u2014 SKI-9](<https://linear.app/21n/document/architecture-and-delivery-plan-ski-9-adopt-mdfn-across-skillplane-web-f69f985bb280>)\n\n## Backlog boundary\n\nThis issue captures a source-backed plan only. It does not authorize implementation, assignment, scheduling, deployment, or publication.",

      "title": "Adopt DataFn in Skillplane's first-party application data path",
      "url": "https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-2/adopt-datafn-in-skillplanes-first-party-application-data-path",
      "description": "## Source\n\nExisting failure-analysis report: `.conduct/issues/2026-08-03-dhu1z1rz-issue.md`\n\n## Problem\n\nSkillplane has a real, authenticated, tenant-filtered DataFn server, schema, and typed client package, but the first-party SvelteKit application does not use it. UI reads and writes currently go through Hono `/api/v1` routes and domain services; MCP operations also use domain services.\n\nDataFn is mounted at `/datafn/*` and passes direct integration and tenant-isolation tests, but no production first-party consumer imports `@skillplane/datafn` or calls `createSkillplaneDatafnClient`. This makes DataFn functionally dormant for product data flows and leaves overlapping read surfaces that can drift.\n\nThis is an architecture-adoption and specification-compliance failure, not evidence that skill creation, save, amend, or publication is broken.\n\n## Intended architecture\n\nDefine and enforce an explicit data-operation ownership matrix:\n\n### DataFn query candidates\n\n* Workspace inventory\n* Skill lists and details\n* Version metadata and history\n* Contexts and knowledge history\n* Notes and note history\n* Reviews\n* Analytics read models\n\n### Domain-command candidates\n\nKeep invariant-heavy operations in Hono/domain services, including:\n\n* Skill creation, draft/version save, amendment, and publication\n* Archive/restore when coupled to bundles\n* Review transitions\n* Invitation delivery and OAuth token issuance\n* Any workflow requiring locks, expected-version checks, idempotency, audit, compensation, or coordinated R2/Postgres state\n\n### DataFn mutation candidates\n\nAdopt only where authorization and the complete operation invariants can be safely expressed in DataFn policy. If the approved set is empty, document that decision explicitly instead of claiming generic mutation adoption.\n\n## Work\n\n* Approve the per-operation ownership matrix before migration\n* Add `@skillplane/datafn` as a production dependency of the SvelteKit app\n* Instantiate `createSkillplaneDatafnClient` using the authenticated session and active workspace namespace\n* Migrate approved first-party reads from duplicate `/api/v1` handlers to DataFn, or introduce one typed application adapter whose canonical read implementation is DataFn\n* Preserve AuthFn-derived actor/workspace context and tenant isolation\n* Retain domain services for invariant-heavy commands\n* Reconcile contradictory `MUST` versus `MAY` language in the specification\n* Consolidate or remove superseded read routes after migration\n* Add validation that fails when DataFn is mounted but unreachable from production code\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n* The SvelteKit application has a production dependency on `@skillplane/datafn`\n* At least one representative authenticated browser flow sends a real `/datafn/query` request\n* All reads approved in the ownership matrix use the documented canonical path\n* Client-supplied tenant identifiers cannot escape the AuthFn-derived active workspace\n* Owner, admin, editor, viewer, and agent permissions remain non-leaking\n* Pagination, search, filtering, refresh, and error states work through the production application\n* DataFn client types remain aligned with the server schema\n* Skill create/save/amend/publish continue to preserve R2/Postgres atomicity, idempotency, concurrency, review, and audit invariants through domain services\n* Static reachability and end-to-end network assertions fail if DataFn exists only as a mounted, test-only service\n* Secret tables and credential material remain unavailable through DataFn\n* Duplicate read handlers are removed or explicitly justified",

      "id": "00eb822a-ebc7-4533-9a23-0cfbce95aa88",

      "title": "Refactor Skillplane into a global control plane and regional workspace cells",
      "url": "https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-13/refactor-skillplane-into-a-global-control-plane-and-regional-workspace",
      "description": "## Executive summary\n\nRefactor Skillplane into a global gateway/control plane plus regional workspace cells while preserving the canonical public endpoints `app.skillplane.dev` and `mcp.skillplane.dev`. Clients, OAuth callbacks, and MCP integrations must not resolve or switch to regional hostnames.\n\nThe gateway/control plane owns globally required identity and workspace-routing state. Each workspace is assigned to exactly one regional cell that owns its tenant data and bundle storage. Requests are routed internally using the AuthFn and DataFn multi-region contracts, with provider-neutral application interfaces and Cloudflare-specific adapters confined to deployment packages.\n\n## Current implementation basis\n\nVerified against current Skillplane branch/remote head `SKI-8` at `3de271619200f9ee45fd31ee056568f8500b7db5`:\n\n* `packages/config/src/index.ts` accepts one `HYPERDRIVE` binding and one `SKILL_BUNDLES` object-storage binding and produces one database/runtime configuration.\n* `packages/api/src/services.ts` constructs AuthFn, DataFn, domain services, and R2 repositories around the same database client and bucket.\n* `packages/auth/src/server.ts` configures AuthFn without its multi-region plugin; `packages/datafn/src/server.ts` configures one DataFn database and derives the namespace from the authenticated workspace.\n* `packages/db/src/schema/domain.ts` co-locates AuthFn identity, workspaces/memberships/invitations/service principals, and workspace content. It uses database foreign keys across those categories.\n* `packages/api/src/tenancy.ts` joins workspace membership directly to `authfn_users` and creates personal workspaces transactionally in the same database.\n* The MCP OAuth implementation stores opaque authorization codes, access tokens, refresh tokens, clients, and consent records in the same PostgreSQL origin.\n* `scripts/render-deploy-config.mjs` and production deployment helpers require exactly one Hyperdrive configuration, one R2 bucket, and one custom-domain route per app/MCP worker.\n* Production issuer/resource are already canonical: `https://app.skillplane.dev` and `https://mcp.skillplane.dev/mcp`.\n\n## Problem\n\nThe current process and relational schema assume every request, user, workspace, skill, OAuth record, and bundle is reachable through one database/storage pair. Adding a second region cannot be solved by DNS alone: clients do not always know the workspace before authentication, OAuth callbacks must retain a stable issuer, users may belong to workspaces in multiple regions, and cross-database foreign keys cannot span regional cells.\n\nA canonical gateway removes regional-hostname resolution from clients, but it becomes a global dependency. If ingress or the authoritative workspace directory is unavailable, healthy cells cannot be reached through the canonical endpoints. The architecture must make this dependency explicit, replicated/cached where safe, observable, and fail-closed rather than silently selecting a region.\n\n## Target architecture\n\n### Global gateway/control plane\n\nThe canonical app and MCP workers terminate public HTTP/TLS, enforce request size and abuse controls, attach correlation identity, and dispatch internally. The global control plane owns the minimum state required before a workspace cell can be selected:\n\n* AuthFn account placement and canonical session/OAuth routing metadata;\n* users and global identity references;\n* workspace directory: workspace ID/slug, owning region, routing epoch, lifecycle state;\n* workspace membership and invitation routing metadata needed to determine authorized workspace access;\n* service-principal/API-key-to-workspace mapping;\n* OAuth client registration, authorization request/code, consent, token family/revocation state, or another explicitly documented globally reachable partition;\n* global publication/search projection needed for unauthenticated or cross-workspace discovery;\n* placement/migration audit records and gateway configuration.\n\nThis is a logical control-plane boundary, not necessarily one primary database. Its backing services must satisfy the documented consistency/availability contract.\n\n### Regional workspace cell\n\nEach cell owns one regional PostgreSQL/DataFn instance and regional object storage for assigned workspaces, including:\n\n* skills, versions, files, contexts, notes, amendments, reviews, publication state, tenant audit/idempotency records, and other workspace-domain tables;\n* bundle objects and digests for those workspaces;\n* cell-local indexes, queues, and outboxes;\n* no authority to assign a workspace to itself without an atomic global placement claim.\n\nA workspace has one writable home region at a time. Active-active writes for one workspace are out of scope.\n\n## Required work\n\n### 1. Create explicit platform interfaces\n\nIntroduce provider-neutral application contracts for:\n\n* `WorkspacePlacementDirectory` with atomic create and compare-and-set move semantics;\n* `RegionalCellRegistry`/dispatcher using adapter-owned internal handles;\n* signed `RoutingAssertion` containing workspace, region, epoch, request ID, expiry, and replay protection;\n* control-plane and cell service factories;\n* global vs regional database clients and object-storage resolvers.\n\nCloudflare implementations may use Workers, Service Bindings, Hyperdrive, R2, Durable Objects, KV, or Queues, but domain/config packages must not import those provider APIs. Document an alternative deployment shape using ordinary HTTP/RPC plus another strongly consistent directory.\n\n### 2. Split the schema by ownership\n\nClassify every current table as global, regional, replicated projection, or migration-only. Remove cross-boundary database foreign keys and replace them with stable opaque IDs plus service-level validation/audit.\n\nPay special attention to:\n\n* personal-workspace creation;\n* membership/invitation acceptance;\n* service-principal issuance/revocation;\n* OAuth authorization, refresh rotation, and token verification;\n* public skill publication/search;\n* audit attribution that references users;\n* idempotency records and concurrency tokens.\n\nAdd contract tests proving referential and authorization invariants after physical separation.\n\n### 3. Route app and MCP requests without client hostname changes\n\nKeep all externally advertised origins canonical. The gateway must derive routing from trusted context:\n\n* pre-auth account lookup for OTP/sign-in via AuthFn;\n* authenticated workspace selection from URL/session/tool input and global membership state;\n* service-principal token mapping;\n* public skill lookup through a global projection or deterministic publication directory.\n\nThe gateway forwards through an internal service adapter. Clients never receive internal regional origins. Unknown, unauthorized, moving, stale, and unavailable states return distinct safe errors.\n\nFor MCP, preserve OAuth resource discovery and token audience at `mcp.skillplane.dev/mcp`; route individual tool calls only after validating the token and requested workspace/skill context.\n\n### 4. Integrate AuthFn and DataFn plugins\n\nAdopt the gateway mode from the AuthFn multi-region issue for canonical identity/OAuth/session routing and the DataFn multi-region issue for workspace namespace placement/execution fencing.\n\nSkillplane-specific code should be thin plugin/config composition:\n\n* AuthFn multi-region runtime adapter and global lookup store;\n* DataFn multi-region placement/directory adapter;\n* request-context bridge that turns validated global identity + workspace membership into a short-lived cell assertion;\n* cell-local service construction from resolved bindings.\n\nDo not fork AuthFn/DataFn routing logic into Skillplane.\n\n### 5. Refactor runtime and deployment configuration\n\nReplace singular assumptions with an explicit topology manifest that identifies the control plane, cells, database/storage bindings, internal destinations, and routing keys. Validate:\n\n* duplicate or unknown region IDs;\n* missing cell/database/bucket bindings;\n* issuer/resource drift from canonical origins;\n* directory credentials and signing-key rotation;\n* no public route exposure for cell-only workers;\n* per-cell least-privilege secrets.\n\nUpdate deployment, smoke, rollback, backup/restore, local development, and disaster-recovery tooling. Generated configuration must support one control plane plus at least two cells.\n\n### 6. Regional object storage and publication\n\nUse workspace-aware bundle keys and resolve the owning bucket from placement. Define whether public bundles remain in-cell behind gateway streaming, are copied to a global publication bucket/CDN, or use a replicated immutable publication layer. Document residency, cache invalidation, digest verification, deletion, and restore behavior.\n\nDo not describe R2 as region-pinned unless the selected Cloudflare product/configuration actually guarantees the required residency; residency must be an explicit verified deployment capability.\n\n### 7. Migration and rollout\n\nUse a staged rollout:\n\n1. add global IDs/directory and routing epoch while remaining single-cell;\n2. split interfaces and remove cross-boundary foreign keys;\n3. run canonical gateway against the original cell;\n4. provision a second cell and place only new test/internal workspaces there;\n5. place new customer workspaces by policy;\n6. build an explicit workspace migration workflow before moving existing workspaces.\n\nMigration must fence writes, copy database and bundles, verify counts/digests/invariants, atomically advance the epoch, warm caches, resume traffic, and retain rollback evidence. Never fail over a workspace to an empty cell merely because its home is unhealthy.\n\n### 8. Reliability, security, and observability\n\nDefine SLOs and runbooks for global ingress, placement directory, each cell, and internal dispatch. Cache signed placement decisions briefly, but fail closed on unknown/stale ownership. Support independent cell deploy/rollback and blast-radius isolation.\n\nEmit safe metrics/logs for routing decisions, directory latency, cache hit, mismatch/retry, cell health, migration phase, cross-region latency, and storage operations. Never log raw OTPs, OAuth secrets, API keys, bearer tokens, or unnecessary email identifiers.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] `app.skillplane.dev` and `mcp.skillplane.dev` remain the only client-required production hosts.\n- [ ] Browser OTP auth, sessions, OAuth authorization/refresh/revocation, MCP calls, and service-principal calls work for workspaces in two cells without client-side regional resolution.\n- [ ] One user can access authorized workspaces in different regions through the same session/canonical origins.\n- [ ] The global directory atomically assigns each workspace to one region and exposes a routing epoch; stale gateways are fenced before cell side effects.\n- [ ] The schema has an approved table-by-table ownership map and no cross-database foreign-key assumptions.\n- [ ] Regional cells cannot trust caller-supplied workspace/region headers; they validate a short-lived signed assertion and local placement epoch.\n- [ ] Public skill retrieval/search has a documented cross-region projection path with tested publication/update/delete semantics.\n- [ ] Bundles for each workspace resolve to the intended regional/global publication storage with digest verification and documented residency guarantees.\n- [ ] A generated/deployed test topology supports one control plane plus two cells using provider-specific adapters behind provider-neutral interfaces.\n- [ ] Directory/control-plane and one-cell outage scenarios have tested safe errors, cache behavior, alerting, and recovery; no request is routed to a random/default cell.\n- [ ] New workspaces can be placed in either cell; existing workspaces remain on the original cell until the migration workflow passes verification.\n- [ ] Workspace migration proves write fencing, database count/invariant checks, bundle digest checks, atomic epoch switch, rollback evidence, and client transparency.\n- [ ] Existing single-cell local development and deployment remain supported during the transition.\n- [ ] Security, conformance, integration, load, and failover tests cover app, MCP, AuthFn, DataFn, and storage boundaries.\n\n## Dependencies\n\nThis product refactor depends on reusable gateway-mode support in AuthFn and namespace-placement/gateway support in DataFn. It should consume those interfaces as plugins/adapters rather than implementing product-local substitutes.\n\n## Non-goals\n\n* Active-active writes for one workspace.\n* Replacing canonical app/MCP origins with public regional hostnames.\n* Coupling Skillplane's domain layer to Cloudflare-only APIs.\n* Automatic data migration or failover without fencing and verification.\n* Making every table globally replicated.",

      "title": "Adapt Skillplane tool contracts for authenticated client compatibility",
      "url": "https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-14/adapt-skillplane-tool-contracts-for-authenticated-client-compatibility",
      "description": "## Executive summary\n\nAdapt Skillplane's McpFn integration so model-visible tool schemas contain only model-owned arguments, trusted caller attribution is injected before validation, workspace selectors are consistent, and pre-handler validation failures are observable and actionable.\n\n## Problem or opportunity\n\nThe production MCP endpoint successfully authenticated a hosted client and advertised the tool catalog, but a request to list available skills failed strict validation before reaching the handler. No tool audit record was created because the failure occurred at the schema boundary.\n\nSkillplane currently exposes a required multi-field `caller` object in its canonical tool schemas. One existing client-specific path removes that field from `tools/list` and restores trusted attribution during `tools/call`; other hosted clients receive the unadapted schema. Skill discovery also uses inconsistent workspace shapes: `skills_list` expects a nested workspace selector while `skills_search` expects a flat workspace identifier. These differences increase the chance that a model generates a valid-looking but incompatible root shape.\n\nThe current validation response reports only a generic additional-properties error at the root and discards the rejected property name, making production diagnosis unnecessarily difficult.\n\n## Expected outcome\n\nEvery supported authenticated client receives an intentional, tested catalog projection. Server-owned attribution comes only from verified request context, tool-selection flows use consistent workspace selectors, and deterministic tests prove that catalog projection and call enrichment remain symmetrical. Failures before handler execution produce safe structured diagnostics and audit evidence.\n\n## Goals\n\n* Resolve client profile from verified authentication context rather than self-reported client metadata.\n* Remove server-owned caller fields from model-visible tool input schemas.\n* Inject trusted caller attribution before strict validation and handler execution.\n* Replace the one-off client adaptation with an explicit, reviewed profile policy.\n* Normalize or deliberately version workspace-selector conventions across discovery tools.\n* Adopt the reusable deterministic profile contract supplied by McpFn.\n* Record redacted pre-handler validation failures with request and profile correlation.\n* Preserve approved tool behavior, tenancy, scopes, authorization, and audit semantics.\n* Add deployed verification for the affected skill-listing journey.\n\n## Non-goals\n\n* Relax `additionalProperties: false` globally.\n* Trust caller attribution supplied by a model or unverified client.\n* Move Skillplane tenancy, grants, approval, or domain policy into McpFn.\n* Rework the authorization-code or token lifecycle.\n* Duplicate protocol conformance coverage.\n* Treat a model-generated evaluation as deterministic proof.\n* Implement unrelated tool catalog redesign.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n* Supported hosted clients receive documented profile-specific `tools/list` output selected from verified request context.\n* Model-visible schemas do not require the server-owned `caller` object.\n* `tools/call` injects authenticated caller attribution before strict validation and ignores or rejects forged caller metadata according to one documented policy.\n* `workspaces_list`, `skills_list`, and `skills_search` support a documented skill-discovery sequence with one consistent workspace-selector convention, or a versioned compatibility plan is approved.\n* A deterministic red/green regression preserves the original list-skills incident's effective `tools/list` schema and redacted rejected `tools/call.params.arguments`, proves the pre-fix path fails, proves the corrected catalog projection plus trusted enrichment reaches the handler and returns the skill list, and retains the malformed call as a negative diagnostic test that names the rejected property.\n* Tests fail when catalog projection and call enrichment become asymmetric.\n* An unexpected root property produces structured diagnostics containing the exact rejected property and validation location without exposing sensitive argument values.\n* A validation failure before handler execution produces a redacted audit or diagnostic event with request correlation.\n* The existing adapted client path and service-principal behavior remain covered.\n* Existing unit, integration, security, MCP contract, conformance, and production smoke gates remain green.\n* As a separate non-deterministic deployed canary, controlled deployed verification runs the original list-skills prompt through a real target-family model using the configured client profile and asserts successful tool execution and the returned response. Hosted inference or API-key access is sufficient; no account or login to the client application is required.\n* Rollback does not silently restore a catalog that exposes server-owned required fields to model clients.\n\n## Dependencies and risks\n\n* Immediate Skillplane compatibility remediation is independent of [MCP-3](https://linear.app/21n/issue/MCP-3/add-deterministic-client-profile-contracts-and-actionable-schema). [MCP-3](https://linear.app/21n/issue/MCP-3/add-deterministic-client-profile-contracts-and-actionable-schema) remains required before replacing the local profile lifecycle with the reusable McpFn profile and schema-diagnostic contract.\n* Related to the completed McpFn runtime adoption, but addresses a newly observed post-adoption compatibility gap.\n* Changing public input schemas can affect cached catalogs and existing clients; rollout and cache invalidation must be explicit.\n* Uniform server-owned attribution is safer, but legacy direct callers may need a bounded migration path.\n* Workspace-selector normalization may be a behavioral schema change and requires compatibility review.\n* Diagnostic events must never record credentials, tokens, full prompts, or sensitive tool arguments.\n\n## Open questions\n\n* Should caller attribution be removed from every public tool schema or only from model-facing projections during a transition?\n* Which existing direct callers still submit caller metadata, and what migration window do they require?\n* Should workspace selection use one nested selector everywhere or one flat identifier everywhere?\n* Where should safe pre-handler validation events be retained and for how long?\n* Which deployed environments must pass the client-profile canary before production rollout?\n\n## Detailed documents\n\n* [Ideation & Product Rationale \u2014 SKI-14](<https://linear.app/21n/document/ideation-and-product-rationale-ski-14-adapt-skillplane-tool-contracts-08f4c3c72edd>)\n* [Architecture & Delivery Plan \u2014 SKI-14](<https://linear.app/21n/document/architecture-and-delivery-plan-ski-14-adapt-skillplane-tool-contracts-95429a5fc9ec>)",

      "description": "## Executive summary\n\nFully adopt McpFn for Skillplane's production MCP runtime, MCP-specific hosted authorization compatibility, regression testing, and official conformance.       "id": "82cd67e3-8311-45ec-9b82-033069d90de4",
      "identifier": "SKI-5",
      "title": "Accept extensible OAuth client metadata for Claude and other MCP clients",
      "url": "https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-5/accept-extensible-oauth-client-metadata-for-claude-and-other-mcp",
      "description": "## Supersession decision \u2014 2026-08-25\n\n**Status: canceled as superseded, not resolved.** The production defect and its security constraints remain valid, but the implementation is no longer tracked as a Skillplane-local OAuth patch.\n\nThe required behavior is now owned by [MCP-2: Make McpFn the batteries-included MCP SDK and quality platform](<https://linear.app/21n/issue/MCP-2/make-mcpfn-the-batteries-included-mcp-sdk-and-quality-platform>) and adopted into Skillplane through [SKI-6: Adopt McpFn for Skillplane MCP runtime, authorization, and quality gates](<https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-6/adopt-mcpfn-for-skillplane-mcp-runtime-authorization-and-quality-gates>).\n\n[SKI-6](https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-6/adopt-mcpfn-for-skillplane-mcp-runtime-authorization-and-quality-gates) cannot complete until this issue\u2019s outcome is proven through the McpFn-backed production path: compatible Claude-shaped metadata reaches authorization code + PKCE and token exchange; ChatGPT is verified independently; extra advertised grants do not become enabled; actual unsupported token grants remain rejected; and the historical failure is covered by deterministic regression plus controlled live evidence.\n\nThe root-cause analysis and security requirements below are retained as migration evidence. If full McpFn adoption is abandoned or cannot meet these acceptance requirements, this issue must be reopened or replaced explicitly.\n\n## Executive summary\n\nMake Skillplane's OAuth Client ID Metadata Document handling interoperable with MCP clients that advertise additional registered grant types while using Skillplane's supported authorization-code flow. The immediate failure is Claude authentication returning `invalid_client` because Claude's metadata includes JWT bearer alongside `authorization_code` and `refresh_token`.\n\n## Problem\n\nSkillplane currently uses the same strict registration validator for two different protocols:\n\n* dynamic client registration, where rejecting grants the authorization server cannot register is reasonable;\n* Client ID Metadata Documents, which are client-owned capability descriptions reusable across authorization servers.\n\nThe shared validator rejects the entire metadata document when any advertised grant is outside Skillplane's allowlist. That blocks a valid authorization-code + PKCE request before consent, even though the unsupported grant is not being requested.\n\nArchived observations show Claude metadata advertised only `authorization_code` and `refresh_token` before the implementation, then added `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer`. The original synthetic tests covered the former shape but not a supported flow plus a registered extension grant.\n\n## Expected outcome\n\nA compliant MCP client can authenticate through authorization code + PKCE whenever its metadata provides a compatible supported path, even if the same metadata advertises additional grants for other authorization servers. Actual unsupported token requests remain rejected at the token endpoint.\n\n## Goals\n\n* Separate Client ID Metadata Document compatibility validation from dynamic-registration policy.\n* Validate the capabilities required by the current authorization request rather than requiring the client's full grant set to equal Skillplane's.\n* Preserve exact client identifier and redirect URI checks, public-client policy, PKCE S256, resource binding, scope validation, and SSRF protections.\n* Return accurate, standards-shaped errors for genuinely incompatible metadata and actual unsupported token grants.\n* Add regression coverage using Claude's current metadata shape and generic registered extension grants.\n* Verify the change through unit, integration, security, and live MCP OAuth testing.\n\n## Non-goals\n\n* Implement JWT bearer token exchange in Skillplane.\n* Expand Skillplane's supported grant types beyond authorization code and refresh token.\n* Relax redirect URI, client identity, scope, resource, PKCE, or token-security controls.\n* Change Claude's published client metadata.\n* Implement or deploy the correction as part of this backlog-capture operation.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n* A metadata document containing `authorization_code`, `refresh_token`, and a registered extension grant can proceed through authorization code + PKCE.\n* A metadata document without a flow compatible with the authorization request is rejected with an accurate error.\n* An actual token request using JWT bearer remains rejected as `unsupported_grant_type`.\n* Dynamic client registration retains an explicit, documented policy for unsupported requested grants.\n* Client metadata and dynamic-registration validation have distinct tests and responsibilities.\n* Claude authentication reaches consent and completes token exchange in a controlled live verification.\n* Existing OAuth security tests remain green.\n* Authorization-server metadata does not advertise grant support Skillplane does not implement.\n* Operational diagnostics distinguish metadata incompatibility from token-endpoint grant rejection without recording sensitive authorization values.\n\n## Dependencies and risks\n\n* Standards interpretation should be checked against MCP authorization 2025-11-25, the Client ID Metadata Document draft version it references, RFC 7591 client metadata, and the JWT bearer grant registration.\n* Broadly ignoring metadata can create security regressions; only unknown or unsupported capability declarations should be tolerated while required identity, redirect, authentication-method, and request-specific constraints remain fail-closed.\n* Client metadata is mutable and fetched remotely, so compatibility tests should include provider-shaped fixtures plus a controlled live contract check.\n* Existing metadata caching and database hydration behavior must not preserve an incompatible or partially validated client.\n\n## Open questions\n\n* Should unknown grant values be ignored, recorded for diagnostics, or rejected unless they are registered OAuth extension grants?\n* Should Client ID Metadata validation require `authorization_code` explicitly or derive compatibility solely from `response_types` and the current request?\n* Should metadata scopes be treated as a client capability set, an upper bound, or ignored in favor of request-time authorization-server scope validation?\n* What cache invalidation and observability are appropriate when a provider changes metadata?\n* Should compatibility contracts cover Claude and other major MCP clients in scheduled production smoke tests?\n\n## Evidence\n\n* Root-cause location: `packages/authfn-mcp-oauth/src/clients.ts`; metadata hydration and dynamic registration both call `validateRegistration`.\n* The grant allowlist rejects any value outside `authorization_code` and `refresh_token`.\n* The token endpoint already independently rejects actual unsupported grants.\n* Existing positive metadata coverage contains exactly Skillplane's supported grants; the negative test only uses a wholly unsupported password grant.",

      "id": "8daff819-16fe-4c7f-aa1b-13012e8c24f9",
      "identifier": "SKI-12",
      "title": "Support Git-hosted skill sources and repository-wide imports",
      "url": "https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-12/support-git-hosted-skill-sources-and-repository-wide-imports",
      "description": "## Executive summary\n\nAllow a Skillplane-managed skill to use a Git-hosted skill file as its source of truth, and allow one Git repository to act as a shared source for multiple skills. Expose source-level grouping so users can see every managed skill derived from a given repository or source configuration.\n\n## Problem or opportunity\n\nSkill authors already maintain canonical skill instructions in Git repositories. Copying those files into Skillplane creates drift, obscures provenance, and makes updates manual. Repository-scale collections such as [vercel-labs/skills](<https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills>) and catalogs surfaced through [skills.sh](<https://skills.sh/>) also need a single import and synchronization model rather than one disconnected setup per skill.\n\nA concrete single-skill example is Diffpanel's repository file at `skills/diffpanel-chapters/SKILL.md`.\n\n## Expected outcome\n\nA workspace can register a Git source once, map one file to one managed skill or discover multiple skills from a repository, synchronize immutable Skillplane versions from exact Git revisions, and inspect all skills grouped by their common source.\n\n## Goals\n\n* Represent a Git source with repository identity, provider, ref policy, credentials where needed, and provenance.\n* Configure an individual managed skill from one Git-hosted `SKILL.md` path.\n* Import or synchronize multiple skills from a repository containing a skill collection.\n* Track each published Skillplane version back to an exact commit and source path.\n* Show and filter all skills associated with the same source.\n* Detect changes, additions, removals, renames, failures, and drift without silently overwriting managed state.\n* Support public repositories first while preserving a secure path for private repositories.\n\n## Non-goals\n\n* Executing arbitrary repository code during import.\n* Treating a mutable branch name alone as immutable provenance.\n* Automatically deleting managed skills when upstream files disappear.\n* General-purpose Git hosting or repository mirroring.\n* Assuming every repository follows one directory layout.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n* A user can configure a single source using repository URL, ref policy, and `SKILL.md` path.\n* A successful synchronization records the resolved commit SHA, source path, content digest, timestamp, and outcome.\n* Repository-wide import discovers supported skills deterministically and previews changes before applying them.\n* One source detail view lists every managed skill sourced from it, including sync and drift status.\n* Repeated synchronization of the same commit and content is idempotent and does not create duplicate versions.\n* Changed content creates a reviewable candidate or published version according to the skill's existing publication policy.\n* Missing, renamed, malformed, or conflicting source files produce explicit non-destructive states.\n* Repository content is treated as untrusted input: path traversal, symlink escape, oversized bundles, unsupported files, and secret exposure are prevented.\n* Existing manually managed skills remain unchanged until explicitly connected to a source.\n* Source removal does not erase immutable Skillplane version history.\n\n## Dependencies and risks\n\n* Existing immutable bundle/version, amendment review, visibility, tenancy, audit, and credential models.\n* Git provider API limits, webhook reliability, force-pushes, deleted refs, and private repository authorization.\n* Repository discovery conventions and conflicts between source metadata and Skillplane metadata.\n* Supply-chain risks from compromised repositories or mutable refs.\n* Scale limits for large monorepos and bulk synchronization.\n\n## Open questions\n\n* Which providers and URL forms are supported first?\n* Are refs pinned to commits, tracked branches/tags, or both?\n* Is synchronization manual, scheduled, webhook-driven, or configurable?\n* What repository layouts and manifests define multiple skills?\n* How are upstream rename and deletion intents confirmed?\n* Can one managed skill combine Git-sourced files with Skillplane-managed overlays?\n* How are forks and repository transfers represented without losing provenance?\n* Should [skills.sh](<http://skills.sh>) be integrated as a catalog/discovery layer, a Git source resolver, or both?\n\n## Supporting documents\n\n* [Ideation & Product Rationale](<https://linear.app/21n/document/ideation-and-product-rationale-ski-12-support-git-hosted-skill-sources-25abc9c35487>)\n* [Architecture & Delivery Plan](<https://linear.app/21n/document/architecture-and-delivery-plan-ski-12-support-git-hosted-skill-sources-20057351abbe>)",

      "id": "9cb0acc8-c438-416f-9ddf-048fcfe1a882",
      "identifier": "SKI-11",
      "title": "Support skill groups and workspace member assignments",
      "url": "https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-11/support-skill-groups-and-workspace-member-assignments",
      "description": "## Executive summary\n\nAdd workspace-level skill groups so Skillplane can organize related skills by domain and associate workspace members with those groups\u2014for example Design, Marketing, Development, and Sales.\n\n## Problem or opportunity\n\nA flat workspace skill catalog does not express which skills belong together or which members should work with a domain-specific collection. As the catalog and workspace membership grow, discovery, onboarding, and administration become harder.\n\n## Expected outcome\n\nWorkspace administrators can define reusable skill groups, associate skills and members with them, and inspect those relationships. Members can quickly find the skills relevant to their domains.\n\n## Goals\n\n* Create, rename, describe, archive, and restore skill groups within a workspace.\n* Associate skills with skill groups.\n* Associate workspace members with skill groups.\n* Show and filter skills and members by group.\n* Preserve workspace isolation, role-based administration, auditability, and deterministic API behavior.\n* Define how group membership interacts with skill visibility and authorization before rollout.\n\n## Non-goals\n\n* Replacing existing workspace roles.\n* Inferring a member's group from job title or behavior.\n* Automatically generating or changing skill content.\n* Implementing organization-wide groups shared across unrelated workspaces unless separately designed.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n* A workspace can maintain domain groups such as Design, Marketing, Development, and Sales.\n* Authorized administrators can add and remove skills and members without duplicate associations.\n* Group detail views expose the associated skills and members; skill/member views expose their groups.\n* Lists and search can filter by group.\n* Archived groups do not silently delete skills, members, or historical audit records.\n* Cross-workspace references are rejected.\n* Every membership change is attributable in audit history.\n* Existing workspaces continue to work without creating groups.\n* Product and API semantics clearly state whether groups are organizational only or affect effective skill access.\n\n## Dependencies and risks\n\n* Existing workspace membership, skill visibility, authorization, and audit models.\n* Risk of accidentally widening access if group membership is treated as a grant.\n* Risk of confusing group membership with workspace role or team ownership.\n* Migration and indexing requirements for existing skills and members.\n* Large groups may require pagination and bulk-operation safeguards.\n\n## Open questions\n\n* Does membership grant skill access, configure defaults, or only categorize and filter?\n* Can a skill and a member belong to multiple groups?\n* Who may administer groups: owners only, or admins as well?\n* Should personal workspaces support groups?\n* How should group removal affect effective access, pinned skills, or agent configurations?\n* Are nested groups needed, or should the first version remain flat?\n\n## Supporting documents\n\n* [Ideation & Product Rationale](<https://linear.app/21n/document/ideation-and-product-rationale-ski-11-support-skill-groups-and-72f905b3b2ce>)\n* [Architecture & Delivery Plan](<https://linear.app/21n/document/architecture-and-delivery-plan-ski-11-support-skill-groups-and-daf45bcc1c17>)",

      "id": "693fecfe-0647-47d3-a152-20874fb3fad5",
      "identifier": "SKI-1",
      "title": "Move service-principal credential authentication to AuthFn API keys",
      "url": "https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-1/move-service-principal-credential-authentication-to-authfn-api-keys",
      "description": "## Context\n\nSkillplane previously owned custom service-principal credential authentication using opaque `sps_...` secrets. AuthFn already provides API-key issuance, hashing, authentication, expiration, and revocation, including a stable API-key actor identity. Skillplane should use that internal capability while continuing to own its service-principal domain model.\n\n## Responsibility split\n\n### AuthFn\n\n* Issue agent credentials.\n* Hash and verify credential secrets.\n* Handle expiration and revocation.\n* Return a stable authenticated actor identity.\n\n### Skillplane\n\n* Map the authenticated actor to a Skillplane service principal.\n* Bind that principal to a workspace.\n* Store and enforce Skillplane-specific roles, scopes, delegation, and domain policy.\n* Record domain audit metadata and lifecycle events.\n* Present credentials to users as Skillplane agent credentials without exposing provider implementation details.\n\nA service principal remains a Skillplane domain entity; only credential lifecycle and authentication are delegated internally.\n\n## Revised product decision\n\nThere is no compatibility window for the former `sps_...` format.\n\n* Removed credentials must fail authentication immediately.\n* The obsolete credential-hash column and fallback verification path must be removed.\n* Existing service-principal records may remain without a usable credential and receive a fresh current credential through the normal rotation action.\n* UI and public service-principal responses must not expose AuthFn provider names, provider enums, or provider-specific identifiers.\n\n## Work\n\n* Define the AuthFn actor-to-Skillplane-service-principal mapping.\n* Replace custom credential verification in the API and MCP authentication paths.\n* Preserve least-privilege workspace, role, scope, delegation, and authorization enforcement.\n* Remove the former credential format, storage, compatibility behavior, migration guide, and migration-as-rotation code.\n* Keep end-user UI and documentation provider-neutral.\n* Avoid exposing raw secrets after the one-time creation or rotation response.\n* Add issuance, authentication, expiration, revocation, removed-format rejection, rotation, authorization, audit, schema, and UI tests.\n* Preserve operator-visible auditability without exposing provider details in the product surface.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n* New agent credentials are issued and authenticated through AuthFn internally.\n* The former `sps_...` credential format is not accepted.\n* `service_principals.credential_hash` and its fallback verification path are removed.\n* Existing service-principal records can receive a fresh current credential through rotation.\n* Skillplane service-principal records continue to own workspace association, role, scopes, delegation, and domain policy.\n* Revoked or expired credentials fail closed.\n* MCP authorization remains least-privilege and is covered by integration and security tests.\n* Credential lifecycle actions remain auditable.\n* The UI and public API do not expose AuthFn provider names or provider-specific identifiers.\n* No raw credential is persisted or returned after its one-time creation or rotation response.",

      "description": "## Executive summary\n\nAfter McpFn publishes the upstream Cloudflare Worker packaging fix, Skillplane must upgrade its McpFn dependencies, remove obsolete or temporary MCP Worker compatibility configuration, and verify the full development topology without changing authentication behavior.\n\n## Problem\n\nSkillplane currently consumes `@mcpfn/auth@0.0.4`, `@mcpfn/core@0.0.4`, and `@mcpfn/testing@0.0.4`. Its MCP Worker deployment exposed the mixed `zod` and `zod/v4` startup failure tracked upstream. Skillplane also retains `allow_eval_during_startup` alongside compatibility date `2026-05-03`; local workerd rejects that combination because the behavior is already default for dates on or after 2025-06-01.\n\nThe Worker should consume the corrected McpFn release and use current Cloudflare configuration without retaining a permanent Zod alias, compatibility shim, or redundant flag.\n\n## Expected outcome\n\nThe full Skillplane development topology deploy path includes the MCP Worker successfully. Skillplane uses the patched published McpFn packages, generated Wrangler configuration is valid for the configured compatibility date, and existing MCP authentication behavior is preserved.\n\n## Goals\n\n* Upgrade Skillplane to the patched McpFn package release.\n* Remove the obsolete `allow_eval_during_startup` compatibility flag from source and generated MCP Worker configurations.\n* Remove any temporary consumer-side Zod alias or workaround once the upstream package fix is available.\n* Validate the rendered topology, Worker bundle execution, and controlled development deployment.\n* Preserve the existing authenticated MCP endpoint behavior.\n\n## Non-goals\n\n* Implementing the upstream McpFn or MCP SDK packaging correction.\n* Changing Skillplane tool contracts, tenant policy, or authentication semantics.\n* Production deployment as part of backlog capture.\n* Broad dependency modernization unrelated to this failure.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n* Skillplane's lockfile resolves the patched published versions of all required McpFn packages.\n* No permanent Skillplane-local `zod/v4` alias or compatibility shim is required.\n* `allow_eval_during_startup` is absent from the source configuration and all rendered topology configurations.\n* The development topology render and deployment checks pass.\n* A real workerd startup test reaches ready state; validation is not limited to Wrangler dry-run bundling.\n* A controlled full development topology deployment includes the MCP Worker without Cloudflare error 10021 or `Class2 is not a constructor`.\n* Smoke validation confirms the deployed MCP endpoint still requires authentication.\n* Validation results clearly distinguish local workerd, Cloudflare development deployment, and production status.\n\n## Dependencies and risks\n\n* Blocked on the upstream McpFn fix and published package release tracked in MCP-4.\n* Generated Wrangler files must be regenerated from their source templates rather than edited only as outputs.\n* A dependency upgrade could carry unrelated behavior changes; review the release diff and run focused MCP tests.\n* Cloudflare upload validation is an external acceptance layer and must be verified separately from local bundling.\n\n## Open questions\n\n* Which patched McpFn version will Skillplane adopt?\n* Are any temporary aliases introduced during incident response present in another branch or deployment environment and therefore need explicit removal?\n* Should the full development topology deployment become a recurring release gate or remain a controlled acceptance check?\n\n## Source context\n\nSupersedes the Skillplane consumer portion of SKI-18: [SKI-18](https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-18/fix-cloudflare-dev-mcp-worker-upload-failure)",

      "description": "## Goal\n\nAfter [AUTH-2](https://linear.app/21n/issue/AUTH-2/expose-placement-bound-auth-context-for-regional-application-data) and [DATA-4](https://linear.app/21n/issue/DATA-4/support-gateway-issued-direct-regional-sync-tickets) are released, move steady-state first-party DataFn reads off the canonical gateway and onto the owning regional DataFn endpoint without weakening authentication, placement fencing, mutation safety, or observability.\n\n## Why\n\n[SKI-13](https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-13/refactor-skillplane-into-a-global-control-plane-and-regional-workspace) gives Skillplane canonical placement-aware routing and [SKI-2](https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-2/adopt-datafn-in-skillplanes-first-party-application-data-path) gives the app one typed DataFn read boundary, but every query still traverses the gateway. That preserves correctness while retaining an avoidable cross-region hop. [AUTH-2](https://linear.app/21n/issue/AUTH-2/expose-placement-bound-auth-context-for-regional-application-data) must first expose placement-bound authenticated context, and [DATA-4](https://linear.app/21n/issue/DATA-4/support-gateway-issued-direct-regional-sync-tickets) must first issue short-lived regional transport tickets. This issue is the Skillplane consumer work after those reusable platform contracts exist.\n\n## Implementation sequence\n\n 1. Consume the AuthFn placement-bound authenticated context rather than deriving a second product-local credential model.\n 2. Add one authenticated canonical DataFn bootstrap call at the existing shared app client boundary.\n 3. Resolve the server-owned registry entry and return only an expiry-bound `{ httpUrl, wsUrl, ticket, regionEpoch, expiresAt }` transport grant.\n 4. Expose dedicated public DataFn-only regional endpoints; keep application, AuthFn, MCP, and administrative cell endpoints private.\n 5. Enforce ticket signature, audience, subject, workspace, region, placement epoch, scopes, TTL, CORS, rate limiting, and DDoS controls at every regional endpoint.\n 6. Extend the Skillplane DataFn client transport with in-memory grant caching, proactive renewal, and canonical re-bootstrap on expiry, region/epoch mismatch, workspace movement, or the standard moved-tenant close/error signal.\n 7. Send query, permitted mutation, pull, push, reconcile, and WebSocket sync traffic directly to the owning region. Keep authentication, bootstrap, placement, public projections, and domain commands on the canonical gateway.\n 8. Add per-phase latency and route-provenance telemetry without logging tickets, cookies, or database URLs.\n 9. Add two-region end-to-end tests proving steady-state DataFn traffic bypasses the gateway, placement changes re-bootstrap safely, and mutations are never ambiguously replayed.\n10. Roll out behind a per-environment/per-workspace flag with canary comparison and instant fallback to canonical gateway transport.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n* The first authenticated DataFn request bootstraps through the canonical gateway and later requests use the ticket-authorized owning-region endpoint until renewal.\n* Regional endpoints accept no session cookie as authority and reject every ticket mismatch or stale placement epoch.\n* A moved workspace re-bootstrap is automatic and never replays an ambiguous mutation.\n* Auth, public pages, R2/domain commands, MCP, and administrative traffic remain canonical.\n* Two-region browser/integration evidence proves steady-state gateway bypass and measures bootstrap, gateway, regional, DataFn phase, and total latency separately.\n* Rollback switches the shared client boundary back to canonical `/datafn` without feature-level changes.\n\n## Dependencies\n\nBlocked by [AUTH-2](https://linear.app/21n/issue/AUTH-2/expose-placement-bound-auth-context-for-regional-application-data) and [DATA-4](https://linear.app/21n/issue/DATA-4/support-gateway-issued-direct-regional-sync-tickets).       "id": "8daff819-16fe-4c7f-aa1b-13012e8c24f9",
      "identifier": "SKI-12",
      "title": "Support Git-hosted skill sources and repository-wide imports",
      "url": "https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-12/support-git-hosted-skill-sources-and-repository-wide-imports",
      "description": "## Executive summary\n\nAllow a Skillplane-managed skill to use a Git-hosted skill file as its source of truth, and allow one Git repository to act as a shared source for multiple skills. Expose source-level grouping so users can see every managed skill derived from a given repository or source configuration.\n\n## Problem or opportunity\n\nSkill authors already maintain canonical skill instructions in Git repositories. Copying those files into Skillplane creates drift, obscures provenance, and makes updates manual. Repository-scale collections such as [vercel-labs/skills](<https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills>) and catalogs surfaced through [skills.sh](<https://skills.sh/>) also need a single import and synchronization model rather than one disconnected setup per skill.\n\nA concrete single-skill example is Diffpanel's repository file at `skills/diffpanel-chapters/SKILL.md`.\n\n## Expected outcome\n\nA workspace can register a Git source once, map one file to one managed skill or discover multiple skills from a repository, synchronize immutable Skillplane versions from exact Git revisions, and inspect all skills grouped by their common source.\n\n## Goals\n\n* Represent a Git source with repository identity, provider, ref policy, credentials where needed, and provenance.\n* Configure an individual managed skill from one Git-hosted `SKILL.md` path.\n* Import or synchronize multiple skills from a repository containing a skill collection.\n* Track each published Skillplane version back to an exact commit and source path.\n* Show and filter all skills associated with the same source.\n* Detect changes, additions, removals, renames, failures, and drift without silently overwriting managed state.\n* Support public repositories first while preserving a secure path for private repositories.\n\n## Non-goals\n\n* Executing arbitrary repository code during import.\n* Treating a mutable branch name alone as immutable provenance.\n* Automatically deleting managed skills when upstream files disappear.\n* General-purpose Git hosting or repository mirroring.\n* Assuming every repository follows one directory layout.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n* A user can configure a single source using repository URL, ref policy, and `SKILL.md` path.\n* A successful synchronization records the resolved commit SHA, source path, content digest, timestamp, and outcome.\n* Repository-wide import discovers supported skills deterministically and previews changes before applying them.\n* One source detail view lists every managed skill sourced from it, including sync and drift status.\n* Repeated synchronization of the same commit and content is idempotent and does not create duplicate versions.\n* Changed content creates a reviewable candidate or published version according to the skill's existing publication policy.\n* Missing, renamed, malformed, or conflicting source files produce explicit non-destructive states.\n* Repository content is treated as untrusted input: path traversal, symlink escape, oversized bundles, unsupported files, and secret exposure are prevented.\n* Existing manually managed skills remain unchanged until explicitly connected to a source.\n* Source removal does not erase immutable Skillplane version history.\n\n## Dependencies and risks\n\n* Existing immutable bundle/version, amendment review, visibility, tenancy, audit, and credential models.\n* Git provider API limits, webhook reliability, force-pushes, deleted refs, and private repository authorization.\n* Repository discovery conventions and conflicts between source metadata and Skillplane metadata.\n* Supply-chain risks from compromised repositories or mutable refs.\n* Scale limits for large monorepos and bulk synchronization.\n\n## Open questions\n\n* Which providers and URL forms are supported first?\n* Are refs pinned to commits, tracked branches/tags, or both?\n* Is synchronization manual, scheduled, webhook-driven, or configurable?\n* What repository layouts and manifests define multiple skills?\n* How are upstream rename and deletion intents confirmed?\n* Can one managed skill combine Git-sourced files with Skillplane-managed overlays?\n* How are forks and repository transfers represented without losing provenance?\n* Should [skills.sh](<http://skills.sh>) be integrated as a catalog/discovery layer, a Git source resolver, or both?\n\n## Supporting documents\n\n* [Ideation & Product Rationale](<https://linear.app/21n/document/ideation-and-product-rationale-ski-12-support-git-hosted-skill-sources-25abc9c35487>)\n* [Architecture & Delivery Plan](<https://linear.app/21n/document/architecture-and-delivery-plan-ski-12-support-git-hosted-skill-sources-20057351abbe>)",

      "title": "Support skill groups and workspace member assignments",
      "url": "https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-11/support-skill-groups-and-workspace-member-assignments",
      "description": "## Executive summary\n\nAdd workspace-level skill groups so Skillplane can organize related skills by domain and associate workspace members with those groups\u2014for example Design, Marketing, Development, and Sales.\n\n## Problem or opportunity\n\nA flat workspace skill catalog does not express which skills belong together or which members should work with a domain-specific collection. As the catalog and workspace membership grow, discovery, onboarding, and administration become harder.\n\n## Expected outcome\n\nWorkspace administrators can define reusable skill groups, associate skills and members with them, and inspect those relationships. Members can quickly find the skills relevant to their domains.\n\n## Goals\n\n* Create, rename, describe, archive, and restore skill groups within a workspace.\n* Associate skills with skill groups.\n* Associate workspace members with skill groups.\n* Show and filter skills and members by group.\n* Preserve workspace isolation, role-based administration, auditability, and deterministic API behavior.\n* Define how group membership interacts with skill visibility and authorization before rollout.\n\n## Non-goals\n\n* Replacing existing workspace roles.\n* Inferring a member's group from job title or behavior.\n* Automatically generating or changing skill content.\n* Implementing organization-wide groups shared across unrelated workspaces unless separately designed.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n* A workspace can maintain domain groups such as Design, Marketing, Development, and Sales.\n* Authorized administrators can add and remove skills and members without duplicate associations.\n* Group detail views expose the associated skills and members; skill/member views expose their groups.\n* Lists and search can filter by group.\n* Archived groups do not silently delete skills, members, or historical audit records.\n* Cross-workspace references are rejected.\n* Every membership change is attributable in audit history.\n* Existing workspaces continue to work without creating groups.\n* Product and API semantics clearly state whether groups are organizational only or affect effective skill access.\n\n## Dependencies and risks\n\n* Existing workspace membership, skill visibility, authorization, and audit models.\n* Risk of accidentally widening access if group membership is treated as a grant.\n* Risk of confusing group membership with workspace role or team ownership.\n* Migration and indexing requirements for existing skills and members.\n* Large groups may require pagination and bulk-operation safeguards.\n\n## Open questions\n\n* Does membership grant skill access, configure defaults, or only categorize and filter?\n* Can a skill and a member belong to multiple groups?\n* Who may administer groups: owners only, or admins as well?\n* Should personal workspaces support groups?\n* How should group removal affect effective access, pinned skills, or agent configurations?\n* Are nested groups needed, or should the first version remain flat?\n\n## Supporting documents\n\n* [Ideation & Product Rationale](<https://linear.app/21n/document/ideation-and-product-rationale-ski-11-support-skill-groups-and-72f905b3b2ce>)\n* [Architecture & Delivery Plan](<https://linear.app/21n/document/architecture-and-delivery-plan-ski-11-support-skill-groups-and-daf45bcc1c17>)",
